title: Adic transport of trace and coherence
statement:
In the situation of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], the same
transport statement holds for the smooth trace of
[def-pur-smooth-trace] and for the coherence statements of
[thm-pur-composition-coherence] and
[thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence].

proof.text: Use the completed coefficient sheaves $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $B_{n,W}=(A_{E,n})_W$ in the situation of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction]. Work with normalized strict semilinear derived systems, not just inverse sequences in the ordinary derived category. By [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons], finite compact supports $F_{f,n}$ and exceptional images $G_{f,n}$ preserve the finite-Tor constructible categories; the coefficient comparison $q$ for $F$ and its mate $b$ for $G$ are coherent equivalences, including the counit equation. Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates] to these enhanced finite operations and coefficient extensions. This gives actual functors $\mathcal F_f\dashv\mathcal G_f$ on cartesian sections, with section units and counits, natural for coherent composition comparisons. [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] realizes them in the derived category of strict coefficient systems, including levelwise pullback, tensor, and the specified exchange maps. All its rings are the actual quotient sheaves $B_{n,W}$, and no flatness of $B_{n+1,W}\to B_{n,W}$ is needed. Use the compact-support composition comparison of [thm-sf-comp-composition] in these simultaneous geometric models. Fix the realizations $\mathcal F_f,\mathcal G_f=\mathcal E_f$ and their evaluation/counit transformations to be the ones specified in [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]; this uses its actual system transformations, not an identification of lifts from equality of evaluations. Thus the subsequent inverse limit uses precisely the exceptional-system realization specified by [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint].

source.place: counit of the realized adjunction; coherent realization of the finite operations

proof.text: Put $T_{f,n}=B_{n,X}(d)[2d]$ and $\Omega_{f,\bullet}=\mathcal G_f\mathbf1_{Y,\bullet}$. The twists and their quotient transitions are those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. At every level, [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] identifies $\Omega_{f,n}$ with $T_{f,n}$ by the unit component of the smooth purity map. [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] makes these components commute with quotient transitions. Both systems have cohomology in the single degree $r=-2d$: exact evaluation and componentwise cohomology in [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension] detect this in the strict system category. Replace either system functorially by its degree-$r$ cohomology system placed in degree $r$: for a complex $C$, the zigzag is $C\leftarrow\tau_{\le r}C\to H^r(C)[-r]$, with the upper truncation using $\ker d^r$ and the second map the quotient by $\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$. Both maps are quasi-isomorphisms because the other cohomology vanishes. The compatible level orientation maps now give an actual isomorphism of cohomology systems. Hence they give $j_f:T_{f,\bullet}\simeq\Omega_{f,\bullet}$ in the derived system category. Moreover, maps between these single-degree systems are determined by their components: after the common shift, use [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] in the abelian category of strict systems, where a sheaf-system map is componentwise. This argument applies only to these single-degree objects; it does not assert faithfulness of arbitrary derived evaluation. Here the unit component is the inverse diagonal orientation, under the canonical unit/tensor identifications of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]: at $K=\mathbf1$, the projection comparison with the tensor unit is the unit identification, so the transpose defining $\theta_{f,\mathbf1}$ is $\epsilon_{f,\mathbf1}$; the adjunction triangle makes its transpose the identity of $\Omega_f$. Consequently the $j_f$ used in Step 3 has the required inverse-diagonal evaluations.

source.place: compatible systems of finite-level maps; choose a coherent orientation before reconstruction

proof.text: For a normalized coefficient system $K_\bullet$, construct $\theta_{f,K_\bullet}:f_\bullet^*K_\bullet\otimes\Omega_{f,\bullet}\to\mathcal G_fK_\bullet$ as the section-adjunction transpose of the defining composite of [def-pur-co-smoothness]: tensor symmetry, inverse compact-support projection map, then $\epsilon_{f,\mathbf1}\otimes1_K$ and the unit identification. These are simultaneous section constructions by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and Step 1. The finite projection map is invertible on this domain by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]; the finite tensor map is invertible by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]. Thus their section maps are invertible, since evaluations detect equivalences. Define $\Gamma_{f,K_\bullet}=\theta_{f,K_\bullet}(1\otimes j_f)\tau$, where $\tau$ is the twist/shift reassociation of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. This is a natural isomorphism of section functors with precisely the finite smooth purity maps as evaluations. Units, counits, tensor evaluation and transposition are actual section maps, rather than independent lifts of their evaluated maps.

source.place: transport included in the same reconstruction; construct its coherent maps

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus] to the reduction/total-limit adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Its actual counit $e_N:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WN\to N$ is a natural isomorphism for normalized systems, and its unit $u_K:K\to\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WK$ is invertible on derived-complete complexes. The extracted lemma contains the effectivity, triangle-identity and derived-Nakayama argument for this precise unit, and the counit/naturality formulas for transported adjunctions and composites. [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] supplies the derived-complete hypothesis on $K$. No equipped common local model is inferred from constructibility.

source.place: counit transport under reconstruction; unit sk-thm-purity-transport Step 2

proof.text: Apply $\mathcal L_X$ to $\Gamma_{f,\mathcal R_YK}$ of Step 3. Its source is $Lf^*K(d)[2d]$ by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Its target is $\mathcal L_X\mathcal E_f\mathcal R_YK$, using the precise chosen realization of Step 1 and [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] identifies this target functor and its counit with the integral exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]: both are right adjoints of the same integral compact-support functor on the stated constructible categories. The resulting map is an isomorphism since $\Gamma$ is one. The natural counit $e$ of Step 4 identifies its reductions with the finite purity maps, so it selects a coherent reconstruction permitted by [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction].

source.place: counit transport under reconstruction; unit sk-thm-purity-transport Step 2

proof.text: For $N=\mathcal R_YK$ and $P=f_\bullet^*N(d)[2d]$, take $a=\Gamma_{f,N}:P\to\mathcal G_fN$ in the transpose formula of [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus]. It identifies the total limit of $\epsilon_{f,N}\circ\mathcal F_f(a)$ with the integral transpose of $\mathcal L_X(a)$. Here integral compact supports are exactly $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_X$ by [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization], and the counit is the integral geometric counit by [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. Thus this transpose is $\epsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(\gamma_{f,K})$, the coefficient-valued trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Naturality gives explicitly $e_{\mathrm{target}(a)}\mathcal R_X\mathcal L_X(a)=a e_{\mathrm{source}(a)}$, so the comparisons insert on both ends and its reductions are exactly the finite traces. Taking $K=\mathbf1_Y$ gives smooth trace. The same lemma's composite comparison identifies total-limit composites with the stated integral operations.

source.place: counit transport under reconstruction; unit sk-thm-purity-transport Step 2

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated of dimensions $d,e$. Use the section comparisons of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates]. Put $W=f_\bullet^*\Omega_{g,\bullet}\otimes\Omega_{f,\bullet}$, $\rho=\theta_{f,\Omega_{g,\bullet}}$, and $\mu=\rho^{-1}c_{g,f,\mathbf1}:\Omega_{gf,\bullet}\simeq W$. Compare $\mu j_{gf}$ and $(f_\bullet^*j_g\otimes j_f)\lambda:T_{gf,\bullet}\to W$, with $\lambda$ the twist/shift identification of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Their evaluations agree by [thm-pur-composition-coherence] at the unit and [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Their source and target are concentrated in degree $-2(d+e)$, since Step 2 identifies the factors with shifted rank-one locally free twists. After this common shift, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies maps with maps in the abelian category of strict systems, where componentwise equality is equality. Hence these orientation maps are equal. This uses faithfulness only for single-degree objects.

source.place: compatible finite-level composition statements; write the orientation and mate argument

proof.text: For arbitrary normalized $K_\bullet$, apply [lem-pur-system-tensor-transpose-composition] in the simultaneous section models of Step 1. Its $\theta$ is exactly the counit-defined tensor map of [def-pur-co-smoothness] used in Step 3. The required projection maps are invertible by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], and $\rho$ and all the $\theta$ used here are invertible by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], with evaluation detection in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The extracted lemma gives $c_{g,f,K}\theta_{gf,K}(1\otimes\mu^{-1})=\theta_{f,\mathcal G_gK}(f_\bullet^*\theta_{g,K}\otimes1)$ as an equation of actual system maps. It supplies the common composite-adjunction transpose, with projection associativity and counit pasting; no equality of arbitrary derived-system maps is inferred from their evaluations.

source.place: compatible finite-level composition statements; write the orientation and mate argument

proof.text:
Insert the orientation equality of Step 7 into the tensor equality of Step 8 and use $\Gamma=\theta(1\otimes j)\tau$ from [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Functoriality of tensor and pullback, with the canonical reassociations, gives the composition equation for $\Gamma$ before inverse limit. Apply $\mathcal L_X$ and the natural composite comparisons of [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus] (Step 6). The equation becomes
$$\gamma_{gf,K}=c_{g,f}^{-1}\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}Lf^*(\gamma_{g,K})(d)[2d],$$
under the canonical twist/shift identification of [thm-pur-composition-coherence]. All comparisons used here are transported from the specified section constructions.

source.place: compatible finite-level composition statements; write the orientation and mate argument

proof.text: For the Cartesian square of [thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence], use exactly the smooth pullback exchange of [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange]. Write $b$ for its canonical pullback/twist reassociation. Its section realization is $\Gamma_{f',v^*K}\,b\,(u^*\Gamma_{f,K})^{-1}$; it is a section map because Step 3 constructs $\Gamma$ and [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] realizes the pullback and tensor comparisons. Its evaluations are the prescribed finite exchanges, not an unspecified extraordinary mate. Multiplying on the right by $u^*\Gamma_{f,K}$ cancels the inverse and gives $\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}u^*\Gamma_{f,K}=\Gamma_{f',v^*K}b$ as an equation of section maps. Applying the strict derived-limit functor, with the integral pullbacks defined in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], gives the required adic commuting square. The base morphism $v$ is arbitrary; no flatness or smoothness of $v$ is used. Together with Steps 4–9 this proves all three transport assertions, with a coherent choice of purity maps realizing the finite ones.
